subject: Pilot extension: escrow/warranty vs. top-up options
messages:
From: Elena Morales <elena@fluxhealth.ai>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Flux Health Finance <finance@fluxhealth.ai>
Date: Wed, 15 Oct 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot wrap-up + runway — extension options

Diego —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. We made good progress on inference latency and team is excited, but we hit a scheduling delay on our model refresh and need another 3 weeks of pilot access. Before I put this through procurement, two quick asks from finance/ops:

1) Can Redwood do a short addendum for 3 weeks instead of crediting token usage? Finance prefers a timeboxed extension rather than additional credits.
2) If we do an addendum, can you include an escrowed performance credit (warranty) that would apply if average latency exceeds the SLA during that window? They want a measurable guardrail.

Attachments: I can share our internal summary if helpful (not attached).

Would appreciate a strawman today so we can escalate.

—Elena
Elena Morales
Head of ML Ops, Flux Health
elena@fluxhealth.ai
From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena@fluxhealth.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Oct 2025 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot wrap-up + runway — extension options

Elena —

Really glad the demo landed well. Short answer: yes, we can do a 3-week timeboxed addendum instead of credits, and we can include a simple performance warranty tied to the same SLA we used in the pilot. Two immediate clarifications so we give you a clean draft for procurement:

- Scope of the addendum: do you want the exact same throughput/endpoint configuration as the current pilot (same model variant + concurrency), or should we size a small burst buffer in case you run heavier batches during testing?
- Warranty mechanics: we usually hold a small performance credit in escrow that automatically applies as a refund if average p95 latency across the addendum window exceeds X ms. We can map the credit to a percentage of the three-week invoice (typical is 10–20%). Is that acceptable?

If that matches your ask I’ll loop in legal/finance and send an addendum PDF + SOW showing the burst buffer option. I’m attaching a draft addendum template and the current SOW spreadsheet for transparency — feel free to share with procurement.

Attachments:
- Pilot-Addendum-v2.pdf (draft addendum; redlines welcome)
- SOW_FluxHealth_v1.xlsx (current SOW + usage assumptions)

I’ll be available on a call this afternoon if you want to run through the numbers.

Best,
Diego Fernandez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Elena Morales <elena@fluxhealth.ai>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 16 Oct 2025 08:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot wrap-up + runway — extension options

Diego —

Thanks — procurement likes the timebox approach. Quick answers:

- Keep the same endpoint config as the pilot; no burst buffer needed for this 3-week run.
- For the warranty, finance is pushing for a fixed-dollar escrow rather than a percentage. They want the escrow to be 12.5% of estimated three-week spend (they find fixed numbers easier to reconcile). If SLA breaches, escrow applied as a credit to the final invoice.

Can you confirm Redwood is comfortable holding an escrow as a separate ledger balance (not an immediate refund) and specify the SLA metric and threshold you’ll measure? Also, Procurement wants the DocuSign flow to be simple — a single signature from Flux Health is fine.

If you can confirm today we’ll route to approvals.

—Elena
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena@fluxhealth.ai>
Cc: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwoodinference.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 18 Oct 2025 15:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot wrap-up + runway — extension options

Elena —

Appreciate the clarity. Redwood can accept a fixed-dollar escrow of 12.5% of the three-week estimate held on our side as a refundable credit balance (we keep it in a reconciliation ledger tied to FLX-3421). If the measured p95 latency for the addendum window exceeds the agreed threshold (we propose p95 > 220ms for this pilot endpoint), we will apply the escrow dollar-for-dollar as a credit on the final invoice. If not, the escrow will be released and applied to the invoice as prepayment.

Key points for the addendum (short bullets for procurement):
- Addendum period: 3 weeks starting on execution date.
- Endpoint config: same as pilot.
- Escrow amount: 12.5% of estimated three-week spend; held by Redwood as ledger credit.
- SLA metric: p95 latency measured at the model endpoint; threshold = 220ms; sampling as per our monitoring hook.
- Remedy: escrow applied as invoice credit if SLA breached; otherwise released as prepayment.

We’ll prepare a single-signature DocuSign addendum (link below) and include the SOW appendix that lists the usage estimate used to calculate escrow. Priyom will follow up with payment instructions and the SOW line items used to compute the estimate.

DocuSign draft: https://app.docusign.com/FLX-3421-addendum

Thanks — let us know if procurement needs any alternate wording on the escrow hold.

Best regards,
Kimberly Park
Head of Commercial Operations, Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com
